<reason>CON won the safety-vs-leverage tradeoff. PRO's leverage and incremental-swap story never overcame CON's core that human retraining dominates switching costs, standards still need mapping, and modular swaps create daily interface breakage and blurred 2 a.m. accountability that poor districts cannot manage. PRO's fallback to stricter standards and stable screens was answered as lab accountability that hides changing clinical logic.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's HL7/FHIR optional-fields rebuttal plus lab-vs-2am follow-through was decisive: compliant systems still fail without mapping, and stable screens hiding different logic is how harm slips through, neutralizing PRO's certification answer.</best_rebuttal>
